t: You're looking at Richmond Terrace, a row of government offices in Whitehall, built as a terrace of houses. Two people tie it to the past. Gwendolen Guinness, later Countess of Iveagh, was born here; she became a Conservative politician and, by marriage, belonged to the Guinness brewing family. And Sir Henry Morton Stanley died here. He's the explorer and journalist famous for finding David Livingstone in Central Africa, and he later sat in Parliament for Lambeth North, from 1895 to 1900.
